resources.string: Disable Certain Other Extension Mod Roles (For Compatibility)

[b][#FF0000]Sabotaged AU Modding[/color][/b], given permission by [b][#87e36b]Chipseq[/color][/b],[nl]has implemented [b][#DDB244]Chaos Tokens[/color][/b] into [b][ColoredMiraOverloadedName][/b],[nl]which can be enabled via a modifier.[nl][nl]Due to this functionality, the original mod is incompatible[nl]with [b][color=#a1e3fe]M[/color][color=#fffca1]i[/color][color=#7975ff]r[/color][color=#5049fe]a[/color] [color=#a1e3fe]O[/color][color=#ffea9f]v[/color][color=#8d89ff]e[/color][color=#665eff]r[/color][color=#5049fe]l[/color][color=#a1e3fe]o[/color][color=#7975ff]a[/color][color=#665eff]d[/color][color=#5049fe]e[/color][color=#3b34db]d[/color][/b].[nl]Please remove the mod from [b][#0000FF]BepInEx/plugins[/color][/b] and[nl]relaunch the game.

[size=4][b][#FF0000]Warning![/color][/b][/size][nl][b]Town of Extra[/b] has been detected.[nl]Some of it's roles have been disabled for compatibility reasons.[nl]You may continue playing.[nl][nl][size=1][#898989]This can be forcefully disabled in the configuration file of [/color][ColoredMiraOverloadedName][#898989].[/color][/size]
Eliminate those who stand in your path.
Kill players by using your dope abilities![nl]Preferably, explode [b]only[/b] in a secluded area.
The Sentinel is a Neutral Killing role that can explode themselves to kill anyone nearby. They may also kill normally, but where's the fun in that?
Gulp down every last one of them.
Use your Gulp ability to swallow players whole![nl]Swallowed players vanish with [b]no body[/b] left behind. They die for good when a meeting is called.

The Abyss is a Neutral Killing role that swallows other players, hiding them from the game entirely. Swallowed players leave no corpse and do not appear in the meeting dead list — until the next meeting is called, at which point they die for good. If the Abyss dies, any swallowed players are released alive.
Swallow a nearby player. They vanish from the map and are hidden until the next meeting.
Use your Erase ability to mark players.[nl]Their role will be wiped at the [b]next meeting[/b], no matter what happens in between.

The Eraser is an Impostor role that can target players and erase their roles. Erased players lose their role at the start of the next meeting — the erase is permanent and cannot be undone, even if the Eraser dies before the meeting. Each erase increases the Erase cooldown. By default, the Eraser cannot erase other Impostors. If a Neutral player is erased, the host can configure whether they become a Crewmate or die outright.
Mark a player for erasure. Their role will be removed at the start of the next meeting.
Use Distort to reel a target toward you.[nl]After a quick kill window, you become invisible for a short time.
The Distorter is an Impostor role that can pull a target toward themselves. After using Distort, they get a brief kill window and then turn invisible for a duration, moving faster while hidden.
Target a player from the menu and pull them toward you.
Mark your prey and strike from anywhere.
Mark a target, then Assassinate to instantly teleport and kill.[nl]Trace marks are left behind, and you turn invisible to escape.

The Ninja is an Impostor-aligned role that can mark a target and later assassinate them from anywhere on the map. When the assassination occurs, the Ninja teleports to the target, kills instantly, and becomes invisible for a short time. Trace markers reveal the teleport origin and destination.
Select a player to mark as your assassination target. Only one target can be marked at a time.
Teleport to your marked target and kill them instantly, leaving traces and leaves behind.
Choose a target and sway the vote.
Choose a target from the Arbiter menu.[nl]If that player is voted out, you gain a faster kill cooldown, an invisibility use, and a speed boost use.

The Arbiter is an Impostor role that selects a target through a GUI. If the target is exiled by vote, the Arbiter gains a faster kill cooldown plus one-time uses for invisibility and a speed boost. The target cannot be changed unless the option allows it.
Choose a target from the player menu.
Become invisible for a short duration.
Gain a speed boost for the remainder of the round.
Take someone's place before they even know it.

Use your Shift ability to target a player.[nl]At the [b]end of the next meeting[/b], you'll swap roles with them — they become the Shifter, and you become whatever they were.[nl]The swap happens [b]even if either of you is dead[/b] before the meeting ends.

The Shifter is a Neutral Benign role that can swap roles with another player. The target must be chosen during the round, and the swap always occurs at the end of the next meeting — the target will not know until after the meeting who shifted with them. The shift is guaranteed even if the Shifter or the target dies before the meeting ends. The player who was shifted becomes the Shifter in their place.
Target a player to swap roles with. The swap takes effect at the end of the next meeting, no matter what.
A killing role with no abilities, and no allies. Good luck!
The Fake-postor is a Neutral Killing role that has no abilites but to kill. Pretty uninteresting, right?
Fool them with a corpse. Make them call it in.
Spawn fake dead bodies near a chosen player.[nl]Get enough bait bodies [b]reported[/b] to win — but don't get caught!

The Baiter is a Neutral Evil role that wins by planting fake dead bodies and having them reported by other players. Each successful report counts toward the required number of baits. The Baiter has no kill ability and must rely entirely on deception to win.
Plant a fake dead body styled after a chosen player at your current position.
Poison them and watch it spread.
Poison a target to turn their name dark green.[nl]The poison is [b]contagious[/b] and spreads when players touch.[nl]Setting determines if meetings save or kill victims.

The Poisoner is an Impostor role that can poison players. Poisoned players have dark green names visible only to Impostors. The poison spreads to healthy players on contact. If a poisoned player's timer runs out, they die. Meetings can either save victims or trigger their deaths.
Poison a nearby player. The poison will spread and eventually kill.
Use Fake Death to die and turn into a ghost.[nl]As a ghost, you can continue killing a limited number of crewmates.[nl]Your ghost kills are silent and deadly.

The Revenant is an Impostor role that can fake its death using the Fake Death button. Once used, the Revenant becomes a ghost but retains the ability to kill a limited number of players. This allows the Revenant to strike from safety, though they can no longer sabotaging or perform other physical tasks.
Instantly die and leave a body behind, turning into a ghost.
Kill a player while in ghost form. You have a limited number of these kills.
Lift votes and stack your influence.
Use Lift on a nearby player to gain a [b]permanent extra vote[/b] each time you lift.
The Lifter is a Crewmate Support role that can lift votes from nearby players. Each lift grants the Lifter a permanent extra vote, stacking for the rest of the game.
Lift a vote from a nearby player to gain a permanent extra vote.
Build a command unit and eliminate threats.

Convert crewmates into Command Specialists.[nl]You and your specialists can kill neutrals and impostors, but killing a crewmate causes you to die.[nl]If you kill an evil target, you can no longer convert.

The Inspector General is a Crewmate Killing role that can convert a limited number of crewmates into Command Specialists. Converting a neutral or impostor kills them instead. If the Inspector General kills a neutral or impostor with their kill button, they lose the ability to convert further.
Attempt to convert a nearby crewmate into a Command Specialist. Neutral or impostor targets die instead.
Kill a neutral or impostor. If you kill a crewmate, you die.
You can kill neutrals and impostors, but killing a crewmate causes you to die.[nl]After killing an evil target, you return to your original role.
Awaken your dormant minds before time runs out, or you will die.[nl]Kill as fast as you can. Each mind that dies weakens the collective.

The Hive Mind is a Neutral Killing role assigned to one person at the start of the game. There are a set amount of "dormant" minds. At the start of the game, the Hive Mind must use the Awaken ability before the countdown reaches 0. If this is not done, the main Hive Mind will let out a scream and die. Once awakened, dormant minds become full on Hive Minds. Kills and cooldowns are shared across the entire collective (if that option is checked), and deaths within the hive = cooldown increases and debuffs on surviving minds.
Kill a player. Kills and cooldowns are shared across all Hive Mind members (if that option is checked)
Awaken the dormant minds, converting them into full on Hive Minds. Must be used before the countdown reaches zero.
Hive Mind Members Know Each Other
Hive Mind Members Know of Deaths
A member of the hive has died!
A member of the hive has made a kill!
⚠ You failed to awaken the Hive Mind in time!
⚠ [player] failed to awaken the Hive Mind in time!

Command Specialists are temporary crewmate killers created by the Inspector General. They may kill neutrals and impostors safely, but die if they kill a crewmate. After killing an evil target, they revert to their original role.
Kill a neutral or impostor. If you kill a crewmate, you die and cannot revert.
